newsitem.title: CHINA: Standard Chartered yuan deposits hit 18 million.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered yuan deposits hit 18 million.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank Plc has gathered about 18 million yuan ($2.17 million) in deposits since it began its local currency operations in Shanghai earlier this month, Standard Chartered Group chief executive Malcolm Williamson said on Monday.
The deposits were from foreign-invested companies located in Shanghai, while foreign-invested firms were also the major customers for local currency loans, Williamson told reporters.
Standard Chartered is one of the nine foreign financial institutions allowed to take deposits and make loans in local currency in Shanghai.
China had previously restricted foreign banks to foreign currency business but it has gradually been opening up the domestic market to outside competition.
It has limited foreign banks to taking deposits from foreign-invested firms in Shanghai.
The funds can be loaned through the domestic currency interbank market, centred in Shanghai, or deposited with the central bank.
Williamson said, however, that Chinese banks in Shanghai were flush with local currency deposits and are not borrowing.
Foreign bankers have been lobbying Chinese financial authorities to allow them to conduct more business in local currency and expand the number of locations where they conduct yuan business.

Williamson was in Shanghai for the opening of Standard Chartered's Pudong district branch. Foreign banks are required to be in Pudong, a new district that China wants to develop, if they wish to conduct local currency business.
